original.title: QA task and promise domain
original.statement_or_definition: A decision task is a published root promise pair (Y,N) of disjoint binary-string sets. A search task replaces the yes/no output bit by an explicit relation R(z,w) and requires an output w satisfying R on each promised instance. Outputs outside the promise have no correctness condition. This is an algorithm-task contract around the root definition, not a replacement promise formalism.
proof_obligations: Make the task input alphabet, encoded instance subset and output relation explicit for every later algorithm.

original.title: Expected query cost from finite execution prefixes
original.statement_or_definition: For a randomized or measured sequential query procedure with finite outcome sets at every step, let T∈N∪{∞} be its total number of oracle calls. For each M≥1, the first M steps define a finite probability experiment and the bounded query variable T_M=min(T,M). Define the expected query cost as E_qry[T]=sup_{M≥1} E[T_M]∈[0,∞]. This is an expected query count, not a worst-case cap; it does not by itself guarantee that the procedure halts in computation time.
proof_obligations: Define each finite-prefix outcome law from the supplied independent random coins and measurement outcome laws. Prove the finite tail identity E[T_M]=Σ_{j=1}^M Pr(T≥j) by writing T_M=Σ_{j=1}^M 1_{T≥j}; then use the supremum as the definition, without applying a finite-space theorem directly to an unbounded variable.

original.title: Quantum query complexity
original.statement_or_definition: The worst-case quantum query cost is the maximum number of designated U_f calls over promised instances of a fixed input length. original.title: Promise-preserving reduction composes with a query solver
original.statement_or_definition: Let R be a root promise-preserving many-one reduction from source instances z to target instances R(z). original.title: One standard query implements one phase query
original.statement_or_definition: Starting the target qubit in |0>, apply X then H to prepare |->=(|0>-|1>)/sqrt(2), invoke the standard bit oracle once, and leave the target in |->; on the address this implements P_f. Thus the conversion uses one oracle query and two nonoracle one-qubit preparation gates in the declared QC gate model. The target preparation is explicit; no generic amplitude-table loading or preprepared target is assumed.
proof_obligations: Use the QC one-qubit gate convention to verify HX|0>=|-> and count exactly one X and one H preparation gate from the zero target. Then compute X^{f(x)}|->=(-1)^{f(x)}|->, extend by linearity to address superpositions, and verify that no f-dependent target garbage remains.

Report one oracle query separately from the two preparation gates; charge them under the QA01 nonoracle gate-cost definition and QC07/QC09 circuit-resource model. This fixed-state construction does not invoke generic amplitude-table preparation.

original.title: Compute-copy-uncompute produces a clean coherent function query
original.statement_or_definition: If a QC reversible-embedding circuit computes f into a designated output while preserving its input and has gate count G, clean workspace, and an inverse circuit of the same count, append bitwise CNOT copies of its b output bits into a fresh target and apply the inverse embedding. If the supplied Boolean circuit has size S, the QC10 reversible-embedding result gives O(S+b) gates and clean workspace; no improved depth follows without its separate fanout schedule.
proof_obligations: Check the reversible embedding’s clean-workspace and exact-inverse hypotheses, show the copied output remains while all embedding registers are inverted, and keep the abstract oracle query count separate from the compiled gate count.

original.title: Classical randomized Simon search needs exponential queries
original.statement_or_definition: Let N=2^n and n≥8. Any worst-case randomized algorithm that outputs the hidden nonzero s with success at least 2/3 requires Ω(2^{n/2}) classical oracle queries. For q distinct queried addresses, put B=binom(q,2) and S=N−1. Under a collision-free adaptive transcript, the posterior is uniform over at least S−B masks. At the jth new query, at most j−1 remaining masks create a collision with a prior address, so the total collision probability is at most B/(S−B). The no-collision transcript permits guessing success at most 1/(S−B), giving average success at most (B+1)/(S−B). In particular, if q≤floor(2^{n/2}/4), then B≤N/32 and this success bound is <2/3. Averaging the same bound over random coins proves the randomized lower bound.
proof_obligations: Prove uniformity of the posterior after each collision-free adaptive transcript because distinct coset labels are assigned uniformly without replacement; at each fresh query count at most j−1 colliding masks among at least S−binom(j−1,2) candidates; sum these conditional bounds to B/(S−B), then bound the no-collision guess probability by 1/(S−B). Apply the fixed cutoff q≤floor(2^{n/2}/4), n≥8, and average over random coins. Separate oracle queries from classical bit cost.

original.title: Finite universal-gate compilation cost for the truncated QFT
original.statement_or_definition: For n≥1 and rational target error 0<η<1, let m=min(n,ceil(log₂(4πn/η))) and compile the truncated circuit with this cutoff. The omitted rotations contribute operator error at most η/2 (or zero if m=n). Let L=O(nm) count the Hadamard and controlled-phase blocks, with final swaps expanded into exact CNOTs. Under QC12’s fixed-arity QSD, exact-CNOT, inverse-closed dense one-qubit alphabet and exact-arithmetic compiler hypotheses, set δ=min(η/(2L), ε₀/2), where ε₀ is the fixed compiler threshold, and compile each one-qubit block and each complete controlled-phase block to projective operator error at most δ. Do not control a phase-minimized subblock. Projective errors telescope to at most η/2 for the truncated circuit and at most η from the exact QFT. The projective-distance output theorem gives total-variation error at most η for every computational-basis output law. The finite gate count is O(nm·log^{3.97}(2nm/η)) including O(nm) exact CNOTs from fixed-arity decompositions and O(n) swap CNOTs. Per-block scalar phases are retained as QC12 metadata: they are harmless for this standalone output law and become relative under outer control, for which this theorem claims no compilation cost. This is an abstract gate-count result under QC12’s exact-arithmetic compiler interface, with no finite-precision target-angle bit-time claim.
proof_obligations: For m=min(n,ceil(log₂(4πn/η))), apply the truncation theorem: the operator error is at most η/2, or zero when m=n.

Let L count the H and complete controlled-phase blocks (L=O(nm)); expand each final SWAP into three exact CNOTs. Since δ=min(η/(2L), ε₀/2) is within the fixed QC12 compiler range, apply its full-block projective corollary to every one- or two-qubit block, compiling each controlled phase as the complete CPθ target and never as a controlled phase-minimized subblock.

Use the triangle inequality for projective operator distance to combine the L gate errors into at most Lδ≤η/2, and combine with the truncation error to obtain projective distance at most η from the exact QFT. Apply thm-qa-projective-operator-closeness-bounds-output-distribution separately to truncation and compilation and use total-variation triangle inequality to obtain η/2+η/2=η.

Track the product of per-block scalar metadata as one whole-circuit scalar; use standalone global-phase invariance for this output law. Do not claim that the scalar can be discarded under outer control or that an outer-controlled QFT is compiled. The cost is O(L·log^{3.97}(1/δ)) one-qubit gates plus exact CNOT terms, hence O(nm·log^{3.97}(2nm/η)) including exact CNOTs; make no finite-precision target-angle bit-time claim.

original.title: Median-amplified spectral estimate
original.statement_or_definition: For Hermitian H with spectrum in [−1,1] and unitary U=e^{iH}, and requested eigenvalue error ε, choose power-of-two Q≥6π/ε, reprepare |ψ⟩ and repeat QPE independently an odd number r of times, unwrap each phase to the promised interval, convert to an eigenvalue, and return the median. For each fixed input eigencomponent, one run is ε-accurate with probability at least 3/4 by the QA2 tail theorem with K=3.
proof_obligations: Show fresh preparations of the same eigencomponent or preserve the system eigenstate between phase-register runs; for a superposition input, state the guarantee conditional on the sampled eigenvalue.
Apply a binomial tail or median lemma to choose r for failure δ and charge every controlled power/simulation.

original.title: Additive spectral-estimation accuracy and cost
original.statement_or_definition: With the injective phase encoding and controlled-power model above, the QA2 tail theorem gives Pr[d(θ,y/Q)≥η]≤1/[2(K−1)] when K=⌊Qη⌋≥2. Taking K=3 yields one-run phase error <3/Q with probability at least 3/4; when H is Hermitian with spectrum in [−1,1] and U=e^{iH}, this gives eigenvalue error <6π/Q. Choose Q≥6π/ε for additive ε accuracy and use O(log(1/δ_fail)) independent runs with median selection to reduce failure to δ_fail. Total cost also includes one supplied state preparation per repetition, plus the sum of controlled U^{2^j} costs (or simulation costs at those times); it is not merely the number of phase qubits.
proof_obligations: Convert circular phase distance to the chosen real eigenvalue interval and include the Lipschitz constant of the inverse phase map.
Apply the QA2 tail theorem with K=3 to obtain success at least 3/4, then derive the median tail from independent runs.
Count actual controlled powers/simulation and classical postprocessing.

proof_obligations: Use a Duhamel path-variation estimate and telescope constant-segment simulation errors; state required uniformity and precision.

original.title: Two-level gapped path
original.statement_or_definition: For a specified 2×2 Hermitian path, compute its minimum gap, derivative norms and JRS runtime bound.

original.title: Gap closing invalidates uniform adiabatic bound
original.statement_or_definition: A two-level path whose gap closes has no positive uniform g; the finite JRS estimate cannot be invoked and an endpoint-following conclusion does not follow from C² regularity alone.
proof_obligations: Give an explicit 2×2 path and compute the gap and transition probability.
